series: Climate Fiscal Policy Brief No. 1.3 · October 2026
title: Converting a VAT into a Destination Carbon Tax

slides.title: Converting a VAT into a Destination Carbon Tax
slides.subtitle: A carbon component in VAT and a forward obligation on energy suppliers in the European Union
slides.message: Price the carbon Europeans consume, wherever it is emitted: a carbon component inside VAT, imports included and exports exempt, while the value part of VAT falls by rule; and an obligation, fixed a decade ahead, on the few suppliers of fuel for homes and vehicles.
slides.author: Stephen J. Stretton · writing in a personal capacity

slides.title: In the VAT chain, each firm pays the carbon price on the carbon it adds, net of prices already paid

points.text: exactly as VAT taxes value added.
the carbon price on the whole supply chain: here 520 kg at €100/t.

points.text: so every tonne bears one price. A revenue-neutral feebate earns no deduction.

slides.source: Stylized example, 2032: carbon price €100/t, ETS price €80/t at the mill. Working paper 1.3, Proposition 3 and Table 1.

slides.title: One published default per product category, the EU production average, applies to every origin
slides.note: Most firms apply the default as they apply a VAT rate. It is generous to imports at first (about 60% of their embodied carbon), which avoids a trade fight; sellers may prove a lower figure.
slides.source: Author's calculation from Eurostat FIGARO (naio_10_fcp_ip4) and env_ac_ghgfp, basic prices, 2022; working paper 1.3, Table 2 and Figure 1.

slides.title: Cutting the value part of VAT by last year's carbon receipts keeps the swap revenue-neutral

points.text: 15% to 10% by 2037 could lose €120 bn or gain €119 bn a year.
the value component ends at 10.8–12.7% in 2037.

slides.source: Carbon price rising €20/t a year to €200/t in 2037. Author's calculation; working paper 1.3, Figure 2 and Table 3.

slides.title: The swap is mildly regressive; returning the fuel obligation per household more than fixes it
header: Swap, net of national VAT cut
slides.note: Net change in taxes, % of household spending; positive is a loss. Poorer households gain less from the VAT cut because more of their budget is exempt rent. Each member state recycles its own receipts, so no money moves between them.
slides.source: €200/tCO₂e, 2022 intensities, 22 member states; Eurostat household budget survey and air emissions accounts. Working paper 1.3, Table 4.

slides.title: The obligation can pass by qualified majority now; the VAT component needs unanimity

points.text: a carbon component changes the harmonized VAT system (Art. 113 TFEU); Art. 192(2)(a) reserves fiscal measures to unanimity too.
it passed as a certificate scheme, and Poland has asked the Court to annul it as primarily fiscal (Case C-512/23).
a national charge per tonne, not a percentage of price, has a defensible claim to fall outside the ban on other turnover taxes (Art. 401, VAT Directive).
an amendment to the ETS Directive, by qualified majority, as ETS2 was.

slides.source: TFEU; Directive 2006/112/EC; Case C-475/03 Banca Popolare di Cremona. Working paper 1.3, Section 9.
